lens:
Options practitioner, level 2: long calls, long puts, cash-secured puts (CSP) and covered calls; no spreads, no naked short options. The fear model is a validated thermometer of volatility and next-day tail risk, not a return predictor, and volatility is what options price. Three consequences shape the design.

(1) Under level 2 every short-volatility trade is long delta (a CSP, or its parity twin the buy-write), so selling rich fear premium fits only a neutral-to-bullish view. A bearish view can only be a long put, which pays on absolute declines, because the account cannot hedge the basket.

(2) There is no historical IV surface, so no family whose edge is purely the variance premium can be validated on 2024-25. The market-level 'sell puts after systemic spikes' trade also has only 7-10 episodes, and its delta leg already failed (the basket bought at M >= 2). I therefore do not propose it on its own. It lives inside family A, made cross-sectional so that its stock-selection edge can be tested.

(3) Every family is gated on its equity signal with the existing engine (RuleFeatures, Variant, beta x basket benchmark, ct_excess_net). The option is an expression rule, fixed now, that spends no Holm budget: it is chosen live from real IV and checked separately. The check is possible because every option is held to expiry. Its P/L then depends only on the realized path, which we have, and the entry IV, which we lack. A price-only replay of the dev events gives the break-even entry-IV multiples, and up to 30 real expired contracts measure the actual multiple.

Richness is measured against the fear model's own regime-implied volatility to expiry (MIV), so model 1 drives both the trade and the instrument. Single-stock variance premia are much smaller than the index's (Bakshi and Kapadia 2003; Carr and Wu 2009; Driessen, Maenhout and Vilkov 2009), so richness is measured, never assumed.

Ranking: A (Holm-eligible), then C (Holm-eligible); B as information only (holm=False).

Every event count below is a signal-side count on the 2024-01-02..2025-12-31 point-in-time outputs and price features, after the no-re-entry walk and the 5-name daily cap. No forward return was computed or viewed, and nothing was written in the repo.

families.name: A. Systemic flush reversal, sold as puts: cash-secured puts on the names a market-wide flush over-sold
families.mechanism:
Liquidity provision under stress. On a market-wide flush, forced and flow-driven selling pushes the most-sold names below value: margin calls, de-risking, and outflows from levered and sector ETFs. Price concessions revert over days (Campbell, Grossman and Wang 1993; Avramov, Chordia and Goyal 2006; Coval and Stafford 2007; Hendershott and Menkveld 2014). They are larger when volatility is high: short-term reversal returns, a proxy for liquidity-provision returns, rise sharply with VIX (Nagel 2012), and funding constraints slow the recovery (Brunnermeier and Pedersen 2009). ETF arbitrage carries non-fundamental shocks into constituents (Ben-David, Franzoni and Moussawi 2018). The reversal sits in the residual relative to the industry, while industry moves themselves carry momentum (Moskowitz and Grinblatt 1999; Da, Liu and Schaumburg 2014; Hameed and Mian 2015). Hence the segment-demeaned beta residual v.

Why sell puts rather than buy shares: the same day leaves short-dated single-stock puts expensive.
- The IV term structure inverts, and short-dated options are then overpriced (Vasquez 2017).
- Net put-buying pressure meets constrained intermediaries (Bollen and Whaley 2004; Garleanu, Pedersen and Poteshman 2009; Chen, Joslin and Ni 2019).
- The variance premium is largest after spikes (Bollerslev, Tauchen and Zhou 2009; Todorov 2010).
- IV far above long-window historical vol predicts low option returns (Goyal and Saretto 2009).
Meanwhile the fear model's panic regime lasts about 2 sessions. A CSP struck a little out of the money collects that premium while staying long a name expected to rebound. This is the systemic-spike put sale, restricted to the names the spike over-sold, so that its edge is testable on equities with many stock-events.
families.execution: Gated test (shares): buy at the open of t+1 (delay 1; delay 2 for the robustness check), equal weight within the day's cohort. The gate reads the calendar-time series ct_excess_net; capital is allocated in 1/H cohorts. Live: for each name, the instrument (CSP, shares or long call) is chosen at the close of t from the Robinhood chain (see options_expression). Option orders go in between 09:45 and 10:30 ET on t+1, as limits at mid, conceding up to a quarter of the quoted spread. An option still unfilled at 10:30 becomes shares at market that day.
families.exit_rule: Shares: sell at the open H sessions after entry. CSP: hold to expiry with no early buy-back. If assigned, sell the shares at the next open; an early assignment is held to the planned expiry and then sold. Call branch: hold to expiry, sell at the expiry-day close if in the money, never exercise. No stops.
families.benchmark: Beta x equal-weight basket (Variant.beta_benchmark=True: trailing 126-session beta, shrunk one third toward 1), on the calendar-time net excess series ct_excess_net; side long; Holm-eligible. Also report the plain-basket excess. The option expression is judged separately against the share version on the same events (see options_expression), not by the gate.
families.predicted_signature:
Gate (c), on the chosen variant's events, with clusters = signal days (gates.ols_cluster):
(i) Dose-response to market stress: the slope of event excess on M_pct_t is positive (Nagel 2012).
(ii) Alpha, not residual beta: in event excess = a + b x basket holding-period return (trades.basket_ret), a > 0 and a is at least half the mean event excess. Shrunk betas understate stress betas, so a rebounding basket alone could fake the edge.
Reported, not gated:
- Front-loaded but not exhausted on day 1: sessions 1-3 carry more than half of the H = 5 excess, and sessions 2-5 at least 30%. This is what lets the family survive the one-day delay.
- For the option: realized variance over the option life below MIV^2, the fast panic decay the CSP needs.
families.expected_events_2024_2025: A1: 274 stock-events on 57 signal days in about 10 episodes. Signal days by M_pct: 25 below 2, 13 in 2-2.5, 19 at 2.5 or above, so the dose-response can be estimated. A2: 271. A3: 156 on 32 days in 7 episodes. A4: 382 on 81 days in 11 episodes. The events are many but cluster within episodes, so the effective sample is nearer the ~57 signal days. With calendar-time daily excess volatility of about 1.5-2% on roughly 150 invested days, a Holm-passing t (~2.2) needs about 1.5-2% beta-adjusted excess per 5-session event. That is plausible only if a Nagel-type stress premium is present. Prior chance of adoption: about 25-35%.
families.main_risks:
(1) Second legs. Flushes cluster, and liquidity providers themselves de-lever (Khandani and Lo 2011; Brunnermeier and Pedersen 2009). The five daily picks lose together, and the CSP premium cushions but does not cap the loss.
(2) Few independent episodes (~10). One fundamental repricing episode can sink the mean, for example a sub-industry hit by a cheaper-model or tariff shock. Segment demeaning helps only across segments.
(3) Residual beta: shrunk trailing betas understate stress betas, so a rebounding basket can look like alpha. Signature (ii) checks this.
(4) The mechanism is front-loaded, so the one-day-delay check is the binding gate.
(5) Hindsight universe: names that fell and never recovered were less likely to be picked as 2026 AI winners. Any buy-the-dip family is biased upward in 2024-26, the holdout included; only the prospective paper test is clean.
(6) If another lens declares the same equity rule, merge them into one Holm slot; the option expression adds no slot.
(7) CSPs are lumpy on high-priced names, IV can collapse before the t+1 open, and early-close sessions read artificially quiet (excluded).

families.name: C. Idiosyncratic intraday flush reversal, sold as puts: cash-secured puts on stock-specific drops that happened during the session, with no own news gap
families.mechanism:
Large price moves without public news reverse, while moves with news drift (Chan 2003; Savor 2012; Pritamani and Singal 2001; Larson and Madura 2003). Firms release scheduled disclosures outside trading hours (Patell and Wolfson 1982). So a stock-specific drop that builds during the session, with no own overnight gap, on a day the market was calm, is more likely flow or a non-fundamental headline, such as block or forced sales or de-risking. Liquidity-driven moves in large, liquid stocks revert (Campbell, Grossman and Wang 1993; Llorente, Michaely, Saar and Wang 2002), and the residual short-term reversal stays robust in recent samples (Da, Liu and Schaumburg 2014).

Why a put sale: after a stock-specific shock the name's IV jumps, but idiosyncratic jumps are far less persistent than diffusive volatility (Andersen, Bollerslev and Diebold 2007). On dev the fear model itself over-forecasts next-day tail risk after idiosyncratic hits by about a third (F5 diagnosis: observed/forecast 0.67, t = -2.1). If the options market also prices the shock as persistent, short-dated puts are rich. The CSP sells that IV while staying long a name expected to revert.
families.execution: Shares at the open of t+1 (delay 1; delay 2 for the robustness check), equal weight within the cohort; the gate reads the calendar-time series ct_excess_net. Live instrument choice and option order timing as in A.
families.exit_rule: Shares: sell at the open H sessions after entry. CSP: hold to expiry; assigned shares are sold at the next open. Call branch as in A. No stops.
variants: C3: C1 plus relvol_t >= 1.5 (volume-confirmed flow), H = 5
families.benchmark: Beta x equal-weight basket, ct_excess_net, side long, Holm-eligible.
families.predicted_signature:
Gate (c):
(i) The information split. Run B's rule (C's filters, but g_seg_t <= -2) as a long contrast at the same H. C's mean beta-adjusted event excess must exceed the contrast's: no-news shocks revert and news shocks do not (Chan 2003; Savor 2012). If news shocks revert too, the edge is a generic reversal, not the declared mechanism, and C fails.
(ii) Front-loaded: sessions 1-3 carry more than half of the H = 5 excess.
Reported for the option expression: realized variance over the option life below MIV^2, the F5 over-forecast that makes the CSP rich.
families.expected_events_2024_2025: C1: 103 stock-events on 83 signal days (2024: 47, 2025: 56), across 61 tickers; the top 5 tickers hold 18% of events. C2: about 100. C3: 73 on 64 days. The events are idiosyncratic and spread out in time, so the effective sample is close to the event count. A Holm-passing t (~2.2) needs roughly 2% beta-adjusted excess per 5-session event, at the top of published no-news reversal magnitudes. Prior chance of adoption: about 15-20%.
families.main_risks:
(1) Misclassification: unscheduled intraday news looks like flow and continues instead of reverting, for example policy headlines, short reports or conference remarks. The gap filter only removes scheduled after-hours releases.
(2) Power: about 100 events need roughly a 2% edge per 5 sessions.
(3) Concentration in volatile mid caps (61 tickers, top 5 holding 18% of events), with wider option spreads.
(4) The same hindsight-universe upward bias as A.
(5) The CSP depends on post-shock IV being rich, which is unproven for single stocks.
(6) The signature depends on B's rule as a contrast. A failure there rejects C even if its excess is positive.

families.name: B. Idiosyncratic news shock, drift, expressed as long puts (information only)
families.execution: Not tradable as shares, because the account cannot short. The gate series uses side short_info with the beta benchmark: beta x basket minus the names, after the same costs, on the calendar-time series. This is the information a put buyer pays for. If ever traded (paper test only), a long put is bought between 09:45 and 10:30 ET on t+1 (see options_expression).
families.exit_rule: Information test: the open H sessions after entry. Put: held to the expiry day and sold at the close. Never exercised, because a put exercise would leave a short the account cannot hold.
families.benchmark: Beta x basket minus the names (side short_info, beta_benchmark=True), on ct_excess_net. Recommended registry.Family(holm=False): reported and used as C's contrast, never adopted from dev.
families.predicted_signature:
(i) Gradual drift: the second half of the holding window carries at least 40% of the excess, because bad news diffuses slowly (Hong, Lim and Stein 2000). This is the opposite of C's front-loading.
(ii) Stronger in less liquid names: the cluster-robust slope of event excess on log 20-session median dollar volume is negative.
families.expected_events_2024_2025: B1: 151 stock-events on 108 signal days (2024: 68, 2025: 83), across 84 tickers; the top 5 hold 13%. B2: 148. B3: 122 on 90 days. A Holm-passing t needs roughly 2.5-3% relative underperformance per 20 sessions, and that is before the put's costs. Prior chance of adoption: below 10%. Declare it holm=False so it does not spend multiple-testing budget.
families.options_expression:
Contract: the long put nearest delta -0.35 (accept -0.25 to -0.45). Expiry: the first listed expiry at least H and at most H+10 sessions after entry, about 4-6 weeks for B1 and B3 and 8-10 weeks for B2. Buy at mid, conceding at most a quarter of the spread, with the same liquidity filters as A.
Buy only if rho <= lambda_P, the put's break-even IV multiple from B's own replay, and rho <= 1 (never pay more than the fear model's own volatility forecast).
Premium at most 0.5% of the account per name.
Judging: the equity information test is necessary but not sufficient, because a put pays on the absolute move. B's replay therefore uses absolute prices, so the basket's drift during the hold is included. The real-contract check uses whatever is left of the 30-contract budget (about 6 contracts).
Rough magnitude: a 5-week 35-delta put at 50% IV costs about 4% of spot, so the stock must fall about 9% in absolute terms to break even at expiry.
Puts are worse than doing nothing whenever the name's relative underperformance is smaller than beta x the basket's rise (the AI-boom drift, which the hindsight universe biases upward), when post-news IV is still elevated, and when the drift is slow (theta decay over 20-40 sessions).
families.main_risks:
(1) Drift has largely disappeared in large, heavily covered names.
(2) The hindsight universe biases bearish signals toward failure.
(3) Puts need absolute declines against a strong basket drift, and no basket hedge is allowed.
(4) Variance premium, theta, and the spread paid on entry.
(5) Low power.
Recommendation: paper-trade the puts prospectively with at most 2% of the account in premium. If the panel insists on exactly one bearish Holm family across lenses, B1 is the one, but expect it to fail.

position_sizing_and_risk:
Sizing mirrors the engine so live tickets match the test. Each adopted family runs a sleeve. Each signal day's cohort gets sleeve/H, split equally across its at most 5 names, and a day with no signal leaves its slice in cash. Suggested sleeves: A 30% and C 20% of the account; B none (information only).

Instruments:
- Shares: the name's allocation.
- CSP: contracts = floor(allocation / (100 x strike)), always fully cash-secured, never on margin. If one contract needs more cash than the allocation (high-priced names), use shares. CSP notional counts at 100% toward every limit, not delta-adjusted, because a CSP's crash loss (strike minus premium) is share-like.
- Long call: dollar delta near the allocation, premium at most 30% of it, the rest in cash.
- Long put (paper only): premium at most 0.5% of the account per name and 2% in total.

Limits:
- per name at most 6% of the account (shares plus CSP notional);
- per segment at most 20%;
- total long exposure across families at most 60%. A's daily picks are correlated and lose together in a second leg down.

No intra-trade stops. Horizons are fixed, a stop in a flush sells at the worst prices, and a CSP's loss is already bounded by its cash. Expect negative skew in the CSP sleeve: many small premium gains and an occasional second-leg loss. Report CVaR(10%), the worst episode and premium-weeks lost, not just Sharpe.

Operations:
- Never hold an option through an earnings date (Robinhood earnings calendar); take shares instead.
- No option orders on early-close sessions or in the first 15 minutes after the open.
- An assigned CSP's shares are sold at the next open. An early assignment is held to the planned expiry and then sold, so the replay stays valid.
- Long options are sold, never exercised: exercising a put would leave a short the account cannot hold.
- If an option order cannot go in on t+1, skip it, since the premium decays after the spike. Do not chase a day later.

The 30 expired contracts are spent only after the equity gate: 12 per adopted family among A and C, with the rest (about 6) for B or live spot checks.

A ticket is labelled high conviction only if all of these hold:
- its family passed the dev gate, including the 25 bps and one-day-delay checks;
- the 2026 holdout agreed;
- for an option, the real-contract richness check passed and the live liquidity, earnings and parity filters pass.
Otherwise the ticket is shown as shares or paper. Separate paper accounting for each expression (shares, CSP, call) on every ticket builds the options track record the backtest cannot provide.
